decisions.reason: As a space navigation and observation camera close to our core optical and sensor knowledge and still marketed on its own page in 2024, it fits our absorptive capacity and remains improvable through our existing R&D base.
This modular space navigation camera is strongly validated by the ESA HERA mission reference and draws directly on capabilities we already master, so it should stay in the portfolio.

The space situational awareness sensor suite builds on our established offer, and its continued dedicated presentation suggests enough strategic and commercial promise for us to keep learning and refining it.

Although market visibility is weaker than for some other launches, the miniaturized space-qualified LiDAR sensor is close to our knowledge base and aligns well with our strategic move toward compact sensors for future spacecraft and small satellites.

A radiation-hard space camera is highly complementary to our heritage in reliable mission-critical imaging, and as a newly launched 2024 product it merits continued commercialization and technical improvement.

The asteroid navigation and imaging camera is a recent product that builds on our existing navigation and imaging competences, so our strong related knowledge and research links justify keeping it while we accumulate mission experience.
